events.reason: Vaginal discharge and pelvic pressure, 20 weeks

documents.title: Obstetrics Visit Note
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Obstetrics & Gynecology
Date of service: 01/21/2026

Leah Martel, 35, G4P1021 at 20w0d by LMP (09/03/2025) and early ultrasound.

Seen for a week of increased vaginal discharge, without pain, itching or odor, and two days of pelvic pressure. No bleeding, cramping or fluid leakage.

OB history: one term vaginal delivery (02/2024) without complication; missed abortion at 19 weeks with D&E (10/2024); left tubal ectopic with laparoscopic left salpingectomy (05/2025). Other history: prior PID, migraine, depression, restless legs, somatic symptom disorder. Medications: sertraline 50 mg, pramipexole 0.125 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan as needed. NKDA.

Exam: vital signs stable. Abdomen: fundal height appropriate for gestational age. Speculum: external cervical os closed; the internal os appears dilated with membranes bulging into it. Tocodynamometry: no contractions.

Labs: prenatal CBC and urinalysis within normal limits.

Assessment: cervical insufficiency at 20 weeks.

Plan: discussed management with the patient and her husband; they elected a physical exam-indicated cerclage, scheduled for 01/23. Pelvic rest. Modified activity at work.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Phone Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Leah called to let me know OB found her cervix opening at 20 weeks yesterday and she's having a cerclage tomorrow. Scared but clear on the plan; husband taking her. No fever, bleeding or contractions. Reviewed that her usual meds are fine to take the night before unless anesthesia says otherwise. Will watch for the OB records.

documents.title: Operative Report: Cervical Cerclage
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of procedure: 01/23/2026

Preoperative diagnosis: cervical insufficiency at 20w2d.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: physical exam-indicated McDonald cerclage.
Anesthesia: spinal.
Findings: membranes reduced above the internal os; cerclage placed at the cervicovaginal junction and tied anteriorly.
Complications: none. Estimated blood loss minimal.
Fetal heart tones present before and after the procedure.
Disposition: discharged home the same day. Pelvic rest, modified activity, return precautions for contractions, bleeding, fluid or fever. Planned cerclage removal at 36 weeks.

Allergies: NKDA.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Work note question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I had a cerclage placed on the 23rd (OB letter should be on its way to you). OB says modified activity, no lifting over 15 lbs and sitting breaks. HR at school wants a letter from 'my doctor.' Does it have to be OB or can it come from you? Sorry, I know it's a silly one.

documents.title: RE: Work note question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not silly at all. I have the OB records now and can write it based on their restrictions. Letter is attached in your portal. If OB changes the restrictions, just let me know and I'll update it.

documents.title: Work Accommodation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Leah Martel is under medical care during her pregnancy. Per her obstetric team, she may continue working with these restrictions until further notice: no lifting over 15 pounds and the ability to sit as needed during the day. Please contact the office with questions.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE
Date of visit: 03/20/2026

CC: fever and right flank pain.

HPI: 35 y/o G4P1021 at 28w2d with a cerclage in place (placed 01/2026 for cervical insufficiency) presents with 2 days of high fevers, chills and constant right flank pain that radiates to the lower abdomen. Nauseated, no vomiting. No contractions, bleeding or leakage of fluid.

PMH: migraine, depression, restless legs, somatic symptom disorder, prior PID, left salpingectomy for ectopic 2025. Meds: sertraline, pramipexole, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan prn. NKDA.

Exam: T 38.8 C (101.8 F), HR 112, BP 125/78. Appears uncomfortable. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen gravid, nontender uterus. Fetal monitoring: baseline 160 bpm, moderate variability, no decelerations.

Data: UA with pyuria and bacteriuria, leukocyte esterase and nitrite positive. CBC: WBC 16.0 with a left shift, Hgb 12.2, platelets 250. Urine culture sent.

Assessment: acute pyelonephritis in pregnancy.

Plan: IV fluids, acetaminophen, IV ceftriaxone. Admitted to the obstetric service for continued fetal monitoring and IV antibiotics.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 03/20/2026  Discharged: 03/22/2026
Diagnosis: acute pyelonephritis at 28 weeks.

Course: treated with IV ceftriaxone. Fever resolved within 48 hours and flank pain improved. Fetal testing reassuring throughout; no contractions. Cerclage intact. Urine culture: E. coli >100,000 CFU/mL, susceptible to ceftriaxone, cefazolin and nitrofurantoin, resistant to ampicillin.

Discharge medications: cephalexin 500 mg by mouth four times daily to complete a 14-day course, then cephalexin 500 mg at bedtime as suppression for the rest of the pregnancy. Continue sertraline 50 mg, pramipexole 0.125 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan as needed.

Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: OB clinic in 1 week; primary care as needed. Return for fever, flank pain, contractions, bleeding or fluid.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video follow-up after admission 3/20-3/22 for pyelonephritis at 28 weeks; ED and discharge summary reviewed, E. coli sensitive to cephalosporins.

Afebrile since the hospital, flank pain gone, eating normally. Taking cephalexin four times a day, a week left, then the nightly dose until delivery. Some mild nausea with the capsules if taken on an empty stomach. Baby moving well; OB saw her yesterday. Mood steady; she's anxious about how many things have gone sideways in this pregnancy but coping, psychiatry visit next week.

Exam limited to video: well appearing, comfortable, speaking easily.

A/P: Pyelonephritis in pregnancy, improving on cephalexin. Take doses with food. Continue suppression per OB. Call for fever, chills or flank pain. Visit with me after delivery.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 05/23/2026  Discharged: 05/25/2026

Patient: Leah Martel, 35, G4P1021 -> G4P2022, admitted at 37w3d.

Presentation: contractions every 5 minutes and rupture of membranes 2 hours before arrival. She also reported an itchy blistering rash for 3 days that began on the trunk and spread to the face and arms and legs.

Prenatal course: cervical insufficiency with McDonald cerclage 01/23, removed 05/13 at 36 weeks. Pyelonephritis at 28 weeks, on cephalexin suppression. Tdap 03/11/2026. Otherwise unremarkable.

Admission exam: T 37.8 C (100.0 F), BP 120/78, HR 88. Clusters of vesicles on erythematous bases over the trunk, face and extremities. Fetal heart tracing reassuring.

Labs: WBC 9.0, Hgb 12.5, platelets 250; ALT 45, AST 40. Vesicle swab VZV PCR detected.

Diagnosis: maternal varicella at delivery.

Course: placed on airborne and contact precautions in a private room. Spontaneous vaginal delivery 05/23/2026 of a healthy liveborn boy, Apgars 8 and 9. Started oral acyclovir. Cephalexin suppression discontinued after delivery. Postpartum course uncomplicated; no respiratory symptoms; afebrile from postpartum day 1.

Newborn: evaluated by pediatrics for perinatal varicella exposure and given varicella-zoster immune globulin; to be followed by the pediatric team. Discharged home with the mother.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: acyclovir 800 mg by mouth five times daily to complete 7 days; sertraline 50 mg daily; pramipexole 0.125 mg nightly; prenatal vitamin daily; sumatriptan 50 mg as needed.
Follow-up: OB postpartum visit; primary care in 2-3 weeks including repeat liver tests. Avoid contact with nonimmune and pregnant people until all lesions are crusted.

documents.title: Phone Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after discharge summary arrived. Pt home with the baby, both doing okay. Rash itchy but all spots scabbing over, no new ones since Tuesday. No cough, shortness of breath, headache or fever. Finishing acyclovir tomorrow. Baby followed by pediatrics. Booked PCP 6/10 with liver tests that day; she'll come once fully crusted and will mask in the lobby. PCP updated.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Postpartum visit, 2.5 weeks after SVD of a boy on 5/23 at 37w3d. Discharge summary reviewed: chickenpox at delivery (VZV PCR positive, ALT 45/AST 40), treated with acyclovir x7 days; newborn got VZIG through pediatrics and is doing well per mom. Cephalexin suppression stopped at delivery. Earlier this pregnancy: cerclage 1/23 for cervical insufficiency, out 5/13; pyelo at 28 weeks.

Now: all lesions crusted by 5/29, mostly faded now, a few pink marks on her back. No fever, cough, shortness of breath. Itch gone. Bleeding light. No urinary symptoms since the pyelo treatment. Sleep is in two-hour pieces. PHQ-9 6, GAD-7 5, no thoughts of harm. Back with psychiatry next week. Sertraline 50, pramipexole 0.125, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan prn. Migraines quiet.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Skin: scattered healed pink macules on the trunk and face, a few with fine scale, no vesicles, no secondary infection. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. No CVA tenderness. Calves soft.

A/P
1. Varicella at delivery, resolved. Now history of varicella. No vaccine needed. Repeat hepatic panel today.
2. Pyelonephritis in pregnancy, resolved.
3. Postpartum: OB 6-week visit booked. Mood screen reassuring; psychiatry follow-up continues.
4. MDD, somatic symptom disorder, RLS, migraine: stable, no changes.
Annual physical in September; Pap/HPV is due this year.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Leah, your liver tests from yesterday are back to normal (ALT 21, AST 19). The small bump at delivery was from the chickenpox and has settled. Nothing more to do. Enjoy that boy.
